subject: Privnet connector TLS negotiation failures after agent upgrade
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T18:22:00Z
Subject: Privnet connector TLS negotiation errors since upgrade

Marcus,

We're seeing repeated control-plane disconnects on our private deployment since we applied the agent image upgrade last night (2028-07-20 02:30 UTC). The controller logs show a stream of TLS handshake failures and close_notify messages; the nodes repeatedly reconnect every ~30-90s, which is causing job restarts and a handful of failed inferences.

Quick details:
- Cluster: hb-prod-01 (privnet)
- Affected agents: 7/12 (mostly in us-west-2 AZ b)
- Symptom: TLS handshake failed, then rapid reconnect.
- First noticed: ~2028-07-20 03:05 UTC after the rolling upgrade

I've attached a small error snippet and uploaded full server logs and a packet capture to our S3 bucket (link below). Can you triage? This is impacting customer-facing latency.

S3 (logs + pcap): s3://healthbridge-uploads/hb-prod-01/20280720/
Attachment: error-snippet.txt

--
Elena Morales
Head of DevOps, HealthBridge AI
elena@healthbridge.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T18:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Privnet connector TLS negotiation errors since upgrade

Thanks for the alert and the S3 pointer, Elena — we see the same symptom pattern in our monitoring. Putting Karthik (runtime) and Soojin (ops) on this.

Initial hypothesis: the agent image pushed in the maintenance window included an OpenSSL/crypto config change that may have altered the preferred cipher suites or SNI behavior. That can cause a transient TLS negotiation mismatch between agents and the control plane if the control plane hasn't picked compatible ciphers.

Immediate asks:
- Can you confirm whether you applied any outbound TLS proxy in front of agents?
- Please confirm whether you can accept a short rolling restart of the agent process for the affected hosts (we'll coordinate one AZ at a time).
- If possible, upload the raw control-plane syslogs and the agent-side /var/log/redwood-agent.log files to the same S3 path. We'll pull pcap as well.

Mitigation we can attempt quickly (with your approval):
1) Pin affected nodes to the previous agent image (the one deployed before 02:30 UTC) — this is the fastest rollback.
2) If rollback isn't possible immediately, we can toggle a compatibility flag on the control plane to re-enable the older cipher set for these connections (short-lived).

We won't change anything without explicit approval — please let us know which mitigation you prefer. I'm available for a 30-min bridge.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T18:46:00Z
Subject: Re: Privnet connector TLS negotiation errors since upgrade

Thanks Marcus. No outbound TLS proxy on our side — just the standard NAT/egress. I authorise a rollback to the previous agent image for the affected hosts; please proceed one AZ at a time and keep me posted. I've also placed the full logs and pcap at s3://healthbridge-uploads/hb-prod-01/20280720/ and granted your team access.

If rollback will take longer than 20 mins, toggle the compatibility flag and we can follow with a proper rollback.

Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
Date: 2028-07-20T19:12:00Z
Subject: Triage: handshake failures look like SNI/cipher fallback mismatch

Team — quick triage notes after pulling the artifacts from the S3 location: server-logs-20280720.tar.gz and handshake-trace-0720.pcap (attached).

Observations:
- The control-plane logs show a high rate of TLS alert(40): close_notify followed by EOF on read.
- The pcap shows multiple ClientHello messages from agents that include TLS1.3 but with a limited cipher list; the server (control plane) responds with an alert immediately in a subset of flows.
- The commonality is agents running image v2.7.4+ (the new image) while healthy agents stayed on v2.7.3. The v2.7.4 build upgraded the openssl provider and removed a legacy fallback that some OS stacks rely on.

Short plan:
1) Execute rollback of agents on the 7 affected hosts to v2.7.3 (rolling AZ-by-AZ).
2) After rollback, monitor handshake success rate for 10 minutes per AZ.
3) If rollback isn't feasible, enable the control-plane compatibility flag for older cipher lists (temporary).

I'll prepare a short runbook and push it to the drive folder; Marcus, can you own coordination with HealthBridge for the rollback window?

Attachments: handshake-trace-0720.pcap

Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T20:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Privnet connector TLS negotiation errors since upgrade

Elena — rollback executed for AZ b (3 hosts) at 2028-07-20T19:50 UTC; observed handshake success rate recover from ~65% to ~99% within 4 minutes after the first host completed restart. Rolled the remaining affected hosts in us-west-2 AZ c by 20:00 UTC and saw stabilization across the cluster.

Timeline (high-level):
- 02:30 UTC: agent v2.7.4 roll started (customer maintenance window)
- ~03:05 UTC: initial handshake failures observed
- 18:22 UTC: HealthBridge opened ticket with error snippet
- 18:38 UTC: Redwood triage engaged
- 19:12 UTC: root cause hypothesis identified (openssl/cipher profile change)
- 19:50 UTC: rollback started (AZ-by-AZ)
- 20:00 UTC: cluster stabilization confirmed

Artifacts & next steps:
- Uploaded evidence (server-logs-20280720.tar.gz, handshake-trace-0720.pcap) to shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folder/1A2b3SharedLogs
- Created JIRA INF-1289 to track RCA and release gating for future agent images
- Proposed postmortem bridge for Monday 2028-07-23 16:00 UTC — will share calendar invite once you confirm availability.

Immediate ask for HealthBridge: please confirm whether you need any SOC2 evidence bundles from this incident (we can export the audit log and timeline). Also let us know if you want us to keep the compatibility flag enabled longer while you schedule additional testing.

We will follow up with a write-up and permanent mitigations (release gating, expanded canary matrix on openssl provider).

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@healthbridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T09:14:00Z
Subject: Re: Privnet connector TLS negotiation errors since upgrade

Thanks for the quick response and the rollback timeline, Marcus / Karthik. Cluster looks stable on our side and latency has returned to normal.

Please go ahead and schedule the postmortem for 2028-07-23 16:00 UTC; I would like to invite our security lead and platform engineer. Also, yes — we will need the SOC2 evidence bundle for our internal auditors.

Appreciate the clear coordination.

— Elena
